title: Presentism as an Empirical Hypothesis
edition: Published-layout copy, Philosophy of Science 80(5), 1101–1111 (2013); not collated against publisher version
role: Target proposal; Brading herself says §4's Newtonian law-constitutive account is not argued in this article.
findings: P1* ties the present's spatiotemporal extent to dynamics and empirical determination. The proposal is explicitly conditional on genuine subsystems; the only system may instead span all history. Newtonian body/collision examples motivate law-constitutive unity, but no shared operational model, record regime, or likelihood comparison is worked out. The local-present bridge from system unity to ontology remains a proposed account requiring elaboration.
limitation: The article states a philosophical/empirical research program, not a completed criterion for subsystem boundaries or a worked physical discriminator.
read_scope: full-text, all 11 pages; no proof reconstruction

title: Physically Locating the Present: A Case of Reading Physics as a Contribution to Philosophy
edition: Published-layout copy, Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part A 50, 13–19 (2015), DOI 10.1016/j.shpsa.2014.09.007; not collated against publisher version
role: Author follow-up and explicit statement of scope/limitations.
findings: Brading restates law-constitutive unity and reframes spacetime as epistemic. She says the proposal needs significant further elaboration; whether dynamics supplies genuine subsystems smaller than all spacetime remains an empirical question. She links the dynamics-first program to Brown 2005 as a possible starting point. No worked subsystem model, common access protocol, or ontology-selecting result is supplied.
limitation: A programmatic follow-up, not an independent physical test or direct answer to the strongest block rival.
read_scope: full-text, all 7 pages; no proof reconstruction

title: Presentism and Relativity
edition: Complete 30-page, 13-section public archive preprint; title page says shorter version forthcoming in BJPS. Do not treat preprint sections/pages as the published edition.
role: Closest direct rival for explanatory priority of spacetime structure; predates Brading and is not a response to her.
findings: §11 argues spacetime geometry explains the shared Lorentz invariance of diverse matter laws, whereas neo-Lorentzian interpretation leaves a common Lorentz invariance as coincidence; draws on symmetry principles and common-cause explanation. Authors explicitly allow relationists to reverse the explanatory direction and acknowledge that the case is not ironclad. This opponent can grant dynamical laws and explanatory considerations, while denying that dynamics alone establishes ontological scope.
limitation: It compares SR interpretations/preferred-frame proposals, not Brading's law-constitutive individuation or empirical local-present criterion.
read_scope: full-text, complete preprint; argument-focused §§4–11, especially §§9–11, archive PDF pp.17–24; no SR proof rederivation
locators: Archive preprint §§9–11, PDF pp.17–24: §9 p.17, §10 p.21, §11 pp.23–24; not published BJPS pagination.

title: Minkowski Space-Time: A Glorious Non-Entity
edition: Complete arXiv v1, submitted 2004-03-17; distinct from 2006 published chapter, not collation-checked
role: Methodological prior art, not a direct Brading critic.
findings: The authors distinguish principle from constructive explanation and compare geometric and dynamical explanatory directions for SR effects. Their discussion treats explanatory status as context-sensitive and acknowledges geometric explanations while questioning whether they are constructive. This is an earlier assumption-sensitive explanatory comparison; it does not supply Brading's local-present bridge or any empirical difference between temporal ontologies.
limitation: 2004 preprint predates Brading 2013; conclusions are not a claim about the 2006 publication without collation.
read_scope: full HTML text; argument-focused §§3–5 (official HTML section locators; no PDF page locator asserted); no proof/derivation audit
locators: Official arXiv:physics/0403088v1 HTML §§3–5, especially §4 explanatory-context comparison and §5 explanatory direction; no PDF page range asserted.
